title: Typed Telemetry Annotations and Backfill Standard
author: Maria Chen
body:
Summary:

This document defines a typed, minimal annotation schema for runtime telemetry emitted by Redwood services and outlines a pragmatic backfill strategy to populate new fields across historical event stores. The goals are: 1) make telemetry self-describing and machine-checked, 2) enable safe, incremental ingestion and enrichment, and 3) reduce accidental schema drift that breaks downstream alerting, dashboards, and cost allocation.

Motivation:

- Over the last two years we have accumulated multiple ad-hoc telemetry conventions (service_tag, source, request_context) that are inconsistently populated.
- Downstream consumers (alerts, cost reports, evals) require stable typed fields to compute SLOs, allocate cost, and run regressions.
- A typed annotation layer reduces runtime parsing errors and enables schema-driven ingestion gates.

Scope:

- Applies to all services that emit production telemetry into the central event bus (kinesis/redwood-telemetry) and to SDKs that ship telemetry helpers (go/redwood-telemetry, python/redwood-telemetry).
- Covers structured event envelopes, metric labels, and prompt/response metadata emitted as request traces or prompt-telemetry records.
- Does NOT change log message text (unstructured logs) or alter raw audit streams; those are out of scope for this backfill.

Core annotation schema (minimal typed set):

We define a conservative set of fields that must be present in every structured telemetry envelope. Fields are strongly typed and validation occurs at ingestion-time. Services may add additional fields under the extensions namespace (extensions.*) but must not mutate core types.

Required fields (typed):

- event_id: string (uuid v4) — unique identifier for the telemetry envelope.
- event_version: string (semantic, e.g. "v1") — version for envelope shape.
- emitted_at: string (RFC3339 timestamp) — time the event was produced by the service.
- service: string (uint8-safe name) — logical service name (e.g. "redwood.runtime.batcher").
- environment: enum [prod, staging, dev, test] — environment marker.
- telemetry_type: enum [metric, trace, prompt-telemetry, audit, heartbeat] — high-level classification.
- schema_id: string — opaque identifier for the payload schema the producer uses (e.g. "pt.v1").
- provenance: enum [generated, sampled, replayed] — describes origin (important for sampling/backfill semantics).
- privacy_level: enum [public, internal, redacted, pii] — consumer-level privacy hint for downstream sinks.

Optional but recommended fields (typed):

- request_id: string — correlates to user-facing request/workflow if available.
- tenant_id: string — multi-tenant identifier where applicable.
- sampling_hint: enum [full, representative, sparse] — suggests ingestion sampling policy for this event.
- numeric_tags: list<string> — dimension keys that are numeric and should be treated as numbers.
- cost_hint_usd: string — small decimal string representing estimated cost for emitting/processing this event (used for cost accounting).

Extensions: producers are allowed to attach arbitrary key/value pairs under the extensions map. Extension keys MUST be namespaced by component (e.g. extensions.batch_coordinator.batch_size). Extension values are free-form, but any extension considered for ingestion aggregation must be registered in the telemetry registry (see Implementation Guide).

Example envelope (JSON):

{
  "event_id": "9b8b2f4a-4d2e-4c39-9f0b-7c6c2f9a6a2b",
  "event_version": "v1",
  "emitted_at": "2026-06-10T15:12:03Z",
  "service": "redwood.runtime.dispatcher",
  "environment": "prod",
  "telemetry_type": "prompt-telemetry",
  "schema_id": "pt.v1",
  "provenance": "generated",
  "privacy_level": "internal",
  "request_id": "req_42e9c",
  "tenant_id": "acct-12345",
  "sampling_hint": "representative",
  "extensions": {
    "dispatcher.queue_depth": "7",
    "dispatcher.variant": "quantized-a"
  }
}

Implementation guide:

1) SDK validators: ship a small schema validator in each telemetry SDK that enforces required fields and canonical types. Validators should run in fast-fail mode in staging and in best-effort mode in prod (log but do not drop by default).

2) Ingestion gates: central ingestion will enforce a soft gate on schema_id and required fields. Events missing required fields are placed into a high-priority repair queue with sampling applied.

3) Registry: maintain a single telemetry registry (git-backed YAML) listing allowed schema_ids, registered extensions, and owners. Example registry entry: 

- schema_id: pt.v1
  owner: eng-serving-runtime
  fields: [event_id, emitted_at, service, telemetry_type, schema_id, provenance, privacy_level]
  allowed_extensions: [dispatcher.*, batch_coordinator.*]
  retention_days: 90

4) Backwards compat: ingestion accepts older event_version values but marks them with provenance: "replayed" when backfilled. Consumers must ignore replayed provenance for production SLO calculations unless explicitly opted-in.

Backfill strategy (principles & phased plan):

Principles:
- Do not break downstream consumers: default ingestion behavior is permissive and always preserves raw payloads.
- Incremental enrichment: prefer emitter-side enrichment where possible; central backfill used as fallback for historical stores.
- Preserve provenance: every enriched record must carry provenance fields that indicate whether a field was populated at production time or during backfill.

Phased plan (timeline ~12 weeks):

Phase 0 — Prep (weeks 0–2):
- Publish this standard and the registry starter.
- SDK owners implement schema validators and opt-in enrichment helpers (go/python).
- Identify top 30 producers by volume and high-value consumers (alerts, billing, evals).

Phase 1 — Opt-in enrichment (weeks 2–5):
- Services add emitter-side fields for required fields.
- Monitor validator logs in staging and set per-service migration dashboards.

Phase 2 — Ingestion soft-gating and repair queue (weeks 5–8):
- Deploy ingestion gate to flag missing fields and route to repair queue.
- Offline repair workers attempt automated enrichment using heuristics (e.g., map legacy service_tag -> service).

Phase 3 — Historical backfill (weeks 8–12):
- Run controlled backfill for 90 days of historical events for high-priority services.
- Backfilled items get provenance: "replayed" and backfill_metadata with job_id and snapshot_time (stored as strings).

Phase 4 — Completion and hard-gate (post week 12):
- For top-30 producers, enable hard-gate enforcement (events missing required fields rejected).
- For remaining producers, maintain soft-gate with exceptions until they reach compliance.

Backfill: technical details and constraints:

- Backfill jobs are batch workloads that read from cold object storage snapshots (S3) and write back augmented events into a replay topic.
- Each backfill job must include: job_id (string), heuristics_version (string), run_timestamp (RFC3339 string).
- Backfill runs must not overwrite original raw records; instead they produce enriched copies and emit a control-event linking original_event_id -> enriched_event_id.

Heuristics used for automated enrichment (examples):

- service inference: map legacy header "X-Service" values to canonical service names using mapping table with confidence scores.
- tenant_id inference: if request_id contains tenant prefix pattern (acct-xxxxx) extract tenant_id.
- privacy tagging: if payload contains PII candidates, mark privacy_level: "redacted" and add redaction_trace with redaction_rule_id.

Operational considerations and SLOs:

- Ingestion validation error rate target: < 0.1% of events dropped due to validation errors after Phase 4.
- Repair queue processing latency: median < 5 minutes, P95 < 30 minutes for operational events.
- Backfill job success rate: 99% of partitions processed without manual intervention.

Alerting and dashboards (minimum set):

- Validator Failure Dashboard: per-service counts of validation errors, top missing fields, first-seen timestamp.
- Backfill Progress: job_id, processed_events, enriched_events, error_count, estimated_time_remaining.
- Provenance Mix: percentage of events with provenance == generated vs replayed by service.

Ownership and governance:

- Telemetry schema steward: eng-platform (primary owner).
- Registry owner: eng-platform (maintains git-backed YAML and merge-protected changes).
- Service owners: must respond to validator alerts and achieve compliance for the services they own.
- Quarterly review: registry and required fields reviewed quarterly by observability working group.

Rollout checklist for service owners:

1) Add SDK validator and populate required fields in staging.
2) Deploy to staging and run for 7 days with validator in fast-fail mode.
3) Address missing field errors and submit a migration ticket to the registry if a required field cannot be produced.
4) Schedule production rollout and verify no regression in downstream consumers.

Appendix A — Example enrichment CLI snippets:

# Validate a local event envelope with the Go SDK validator
redwood-telemetry validate --file sample-event.json --schema pt.v1

# Run a repair worker over a small snapshot (dry-run)
backfill-runner --snapshot s3://telemetry/snapshots/2026-06-01 --heuristics v1 --dry-run

Appendix B — Example mapping rules (extract):

- legacy_header_X-Service: 
  mapping:
    "dispatcher-v1": redwood.runtime.dispatcher
    "batcher-old": redwood.runtime.batcher
  confidence_threshold: 0.7

Related work and references:

- See telemetry registry starter: /git/telemetry/registry/README.md
- See prompt-telemetry privacy guidelines: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/prompt-telemetry-hash-sampling-privacy-guardrail-2026
- See ingestion gate design: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/ingestion-gate-implementation

Questions, exceptions, and extension requests should be submitted as PRs to the telemetry registry repository and assigned to the eng-platform on-call.
